- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is trending up.
- Overshoots after spikes (especially >80) are common; cap forecast at +5% above peak unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct; apply slight upward bias to counteract.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overreact to short-term sentiment; dampen momentum by 10–15% if sentiment is volatile or mixed.
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative within 3 days, reduce forecast slope; avoid sharp downward revisions unless confirmed by price action.
